patients.summary: Financial analyst in his thirties with ulcerative colitis since 2015 on mesalamine, followed by an outside GI group. Joins in 2022; primary sclerosing cholangitis is found on MRCP in October 2025, and worsening cholestasis in spring 2026 leads to ERCP dilation of a dominant bile duct stricture with negative brushings.

documents.title: New patient paperwork
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, I filled out the intake forms online and signed the records release for my old primary care office. I have my first appointment on 9/12. I see a GI doctor every year for colitis, should I bring anything from them or will you request those too? Thanks, Austin

documents.title: RE: New patient paperwork
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Hi Austin, got your forms and the release, thank you. We faxed the request to your prior primary care office this morning. For GI, just bring your current medication bottle or a photo of the label and the name of the practice; the doctor will ask GI for notes if needed. See you on the 12th at 9:00. Please arrive 10 minutes early to scan your insurance card.

conditions.label: Ulcerative colitis
conditions.note: Diagnosed 2015 by outside GI; on mesalamine since.

medications.drug: mesalamine 1200 MG Delayed Release Oral Tablet
medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
New patient, 30M, moving his primary care here. Previous PCP was fine, wanted easier access. Works as a financial analyst, long weeks around quarter close.

UC: diagnosed 2015, around age 23. Has been on mesalamine 1.2 g twice a day ever since. Followed by an outside GI group, sees them about once a year and they do his GI labs. Says he has been in remission a long time, no bleeding, normal stools, no abdominal pain. Takes the mesalamine reliably. GI refills it.

No other medical problems. No surgeries. NKDA.

Family: maternal grandmother had UC. Father has primary sclerosing cholangitis. Mother has autoimmune hypothyroidism.

Social: never smoked, does not drink at all, no drugs. Lives in Easthampton. Exercises a few times a week.

ROS: negative except as above. No fatigue, no itching, no weight change.

Exam: well appearing. Vitals as charted. HEENT unremarkable, no scleral icterus. Neck supple, no adenopathy. Heart regular rate and rhythm, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no organomegaly. No edema. Skin without rash.

A/P
1. Ulcerative colitis, in remission per patient on mesalamine. Continue with GI. Will request their most recent note. Mesalamine needs renal function checked; doing a BMP today.
2. Health maintenance: CBC, BMP, lipids. HIV and hep C screening today, he agrees. Tdap given, no record of one in the last 10 years. Flu and COVID boosters next month when available. PHQ-2 0.
3. Return in a year for a physical, sooner as needed. He has my cell for questions.

documents.title: Your recent lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Austin, your blood counts, kidney function, electrolytes and cholesterol all look good. HIV and hepatitis C screens were nonreactive, which is what we expected; no need to repeat those unless something changes. Kidney numbers are the main thing we watch on mesalamine and yours are normal.

documents.title: RE: Your recent lab results
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Great, thanks for the quick turnaround.

events.reason: Records from prior primary care office

documents.title: Prior Primary Care Records
documents.author: outside primary care
documents.body:
Records packet, 14 pages, faxed by prior primary care office in response to release dated 08/30/2022.

Contents: annual exams 2018 through 2021, immunization record, medication list, labs.

Problem list: ulcerative colitis, managed by gastroenterology.
Medications: mesalamine DR 1.2 g twice daily (prescribed by GI).
Allergies: NKDA.

Annual exams each unremarkable; weight stable in the high 70s kg; blood pressure normal at each visit. Basic metabolic panels and blood counts in 2019 and 2021 within normal limits. Immunizations listed: childhood series complete, influenza in most years, COVID-19 primary series 2021. No Tdap recorded since adolescence.

Reviewed and scanned to chart. Nothing outstanding. -- MA

documents.title: Immunization Visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Here after work for flu and bivalent COVID booster. Screening questions negative. Flu vaccine 0.5 mL IM left deltoid. Pfizer bivalent 0.3 mL IM right deltoid. VIS given for both. Waited 15 minutes, no reaction. Told him a sore arm or a tired day afterward is common.

documents.title: Pharmacy Refill Request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Fax from pharmacy requesting refill of mesalamine DR 1.2 g, 1 tab BID, #180. Prescriber on the bottle is his GI. Called pharmacy, told them to send to GI office; we do not manage this one. Pharmacy said they had sent to us because GI's fax line was busy. Patient has 6 days left. Left a message for patient letting him know.

documents.title: RE: Pharmacy Refill Request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Patient called back, GI sent the refill this morning, he picked it up. Closing.

documents.title: Immunization Visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Hep B series, dose 1 of 2 (Heplisav-B), per PCP recommendation for all adults under 60; no prior hep B vaccine on his records. 0.5 mL IM left deltoid. VIS reviewed. No reaction during 15 minute wait. Dose 2 due in 4 weeks, booked for 4/13.

documents.title: Immunization Visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Heplisav-B dose 2 of 2, 0.5 mL IM right deltoid. Said the first one left his arm sore for a day, nothing else. Observed, fine. Series complete.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Early slot before work. Feeling well. UC quiet, no bleeding or urgency, on mesalamine 1.2 g BID, saw GI earlier this year and everything was fine per him. Busy at work but sleeping ok. Running and some weights.

Meds: mesalamine DR 1.2 g BID. NKDA.
Never smoker, no alcohol.

Exam: well, no distress. No scleral icterus. Neck no nodes or thyromegaly. Heart RRR without murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft and nontender, no masses or organomegaly. No edema. Skin normal.

PHQ-2 0.

A/P
UC in remission, GI following. BMP for mesalamine, CBC, lipids today.
Hep B series done in the spring. Flu and COVID next month.
RTC 1 year.

documents.title: Lab results from your physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Labs from Tuesday are all normal, kidneys included. Cholesterol is fine. Nothing to do.

documents.title: Immunization Visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Lunch-hour visit for flu and the 2023-24 COVID vaccine. No fever today, no prior reactions besides a sore arm. Flu 0.5 mL IM L deltoid, Pfizer 2023-24 formula 0.3 mL IM R deltoid. VIS provided. 15 min observation without problems.
